authoredSolutions.48: Statement I is true: in a Frenkel defect an ion leaves its lattice site (creating a vacancy) and occupies an interstitial site, so it is both a vacancy and an interstitial defect. authoredSolutions.50: Free-radical bromination is highly selective for the weakest (tertiary) C–H bond. Isobutane has one tertiary hydrogen, so \(Br_2\)/light abstracts it preferentially, giving 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl bromide) as the major product. Hence option (D).

authoredSolutions.80: For the implication to be false, the antecedent must be true and the consequent \(p\land q\) false. From \(\sim r\) true, \(r=F\); then \(q\to r\) true forces \(q=F\); and \(p\lor q\) true then forces \(p=T\). These give \(p\land q=F\), so the implication is indeed false. Hence \(p,q,r=T,F,F\) — option (C).

Write \(z=\frac{1-i\sqrt{3}}{2}=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}-i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\), so \(|z|=1\) and \(\frac{1}{z}=\cos\frac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\). Then
\[z^{n}+\frac{1}{z^{n}}=2\cos\frac{n\pi}{3}.\]
Hence each bracket cubed is \(\left(z^{n}+\frac{1}{z^{n}}\right)^{3}=8\cos^{3}\frac{n\pi}{3}\). For \(n=1,2,\ldots,6\) these values are \(1,-1,-8,-1,1,8\), which sum to \(0\), and the pattern repeats every \(6\) terms. Over \(n=1\) to \(18\) (three periods) the total is \(0\); the remaining \(n=19,20,21\) repeat \(n=1,2,3\), giving \(1-1-8=-8\).
\[21+\sum_{n=1}^{21}\left(z^{n}+\frac{1}{z^{n}}\right)^{3}=21+(-8)=13.\]

Combine the left side:
\[\frac{2}{x-1}-\frac{1}{x-2}=\frac{2(x-2)-(x-1)}{(x-1)(x-2)}=\frac{x-3}{(x-1)(x-2)}=\frac{2}{k}.\]
Cross-multiplying, \(k(x-3)=2(x-1)(x-2)=2x^{2}-6x+4\), i.e.
\[2x^{2}-(6+k)x+(4+3k)=0.\]
No real roots requires discriminant \(<0\):
\[(6+k)^{2}-8(4+3k)=k^{2}-12k+4<0\Rightarrow 6-4\sqrt{2}<k<6+4\sqrt{2}.\]
Since \(6-4\sqrt{2}\approx 0.34\) and \(6+4\sqrt{2}\approx 11.66\), the integers \(k\neq0\) are \(1,2,\ldots,11\).
\[\sum_{k=1}^{11}k=\frac{11\cdot 12}{2}=66.\]

Let the circle's circumference be \(k\), so the square's perimeter is \(36-k\). Then side \(=\frac{36-k}{4}\) and radius \(=\frac{k}{2\pi}\), giving total area
\[A=\left(\frac{36-k}{4}\right)^{2}+\frac{k^{2}}{4\pi}.\]
Set \(\frac{dA}{dk}=0\):
\[-\frac{36-k}{8}+\frac{k}{2\pi}=0\Rightarrow 8k=2\pi(36-k)\Rightarrow k=\frac{36\pi}{4+\pi}.\]
Therefore
\[\left(\frac{4}{\pi}+1\right)k=\frac{4+\pi}{\pi}\cdot\frac{36\pi}{4+\pi}=36.\]

Let the point be \((x,y)\). The sum of squared distances from \((0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\) is
\[\big(4x^{2}-4x+2\big)+\big(4y^{2}-4y+2\big)=18.\]
Thus \(4x^{2}+4y^{2}-4x-4y+4=18\), i.e.
\[x^{2}+y^{2}-x-y-\tfrac{7}{2}=0.\]
This circle has centre \(\left(\tfrac12,\tfrac12\right)\) and
\[r^{2}=\tfrac14+\tfrac14+\tfrac72=4\Rightarrow r=2,\ d=2r=4.\]
\[d^{2}=16.\]

The number is even, so the units digit is \(0,4,\) or \(6\).
Units \(=0\): hundreds from \(\{1,3,4,6,7\}\) gives \(5\) choices, tens from the remaining \(4\): \(5\times4=20\).
Units \(=4\): hundreds cannot be \(0\), leaving \(\{1,3,6,7\}\) i.e. \(4\) choices, tens from remaining \(4\): \(4\times4=16\).
Units \(=6\): similarly \(4\times4=16\).
\[\text{Total}=20+16+16=52.\]

For \(x\le 0\), \(f(0)=a\sin\frac{\pi}{2}(0-1)=a\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=-a\).
For \(x>0\), use \(\tan 2x-\sin 2x=\sin 2x\cdot\frac{1-\cos 2x}{\cos 2x}\). As \(x\to0^{+}\), \(\sin 2x\approx 2x\), \(1-\cos 2x\approx 2x^{2}\), \(\cos 2x\to1\), so the numerator \(\approx 4x^{3}\) and
\[\lim_{x\to0^{+}}\frac{\tan 2x-\sin 2x}{bx^{3}}=\frac{4}{b}.\]
Continuity at \(0\) gives \(-a=\dfrac{4}{b}\Rightarrow ab=-4\). Hence
\[10-ab=10-(-4)=14.\]
